name: Genspark
tagline: A "Super Agent" that orchestrates 9 blended LLMs and 80+ tools to research, build slides/sheets, place phone calls and browse the web from one prompt.
verdict: Genspark is the best-funded and most heavily used general-purpose agent in this category — $535M raised, a $2.6B valuation and roughly $250M in annualized revenue back real, measurable traction, not just a viral demo. Its mixture-of-agents design, blending nine specialized models with cross-checking to cut hallucination, is a genuine architectural bet rather than a single-model wrapper, and its surface is unusually broad: cited research reports, slide decks, live spreadsheets, real outbound phone calls and autonomous browsing all live in one workspace. The honest tradeoffs are real too: independent reviews consistently flag the credit system's fine print — a session cap undermining "unlimited" chat, credits that don't roll over and debit even on failed runs, and a zero-credit promotion with a hard December 2026 expiry — and, unlike its closest rival Manus, no source found documents a public developer API, so there is no confirmed way to build Genspark into your own software today. Pick Genspark if you want one broad, well-funded workspace for research-to-deliverable work and don't need to automate it programmatically; pick Manus instead if a developer API and code-execution/browser-operator depth matter more than Genspark's wider consumer surface.
